description: The Earth's surface is primarily divided into the lithosphere (land) and hydrosphere (water). It comprises significant geographical features such as mountains, plateaus, plains, continents, and oceans.

sections.title: Major Landforms of the Earth
sections.description: The natural physical features of the Earth's surface, classified primarily based on their elevation, slope, and formation process.

key_concepts.explanation: A natural elevation of the Earth's surface with a broad base and a small summit. Based on their formation, they are classified into Fold, Block, and Volcanic mountains.
An elevated flat land or a flat-topped tableland standing above the surrounding area. They are generally very rich in mineral deposits.
Large stretches of flat land generally formed by the deposition of alluvium brought down by rivers and their tributaries.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Located in Asia and Europe respectively.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: They are examples of Young Fold Mountains characterized by rugged relief and high conical peaks.
It is the highest plateau in the world, often referred to as the 'Roof of the World'.

important_facts.fact: Mount Kilimanjaro in Africa and Mount Fujiyama in Japan are prominent examples of Volcanic Mountains formed by volcanic activity.

sections.title: Continental Drift and Plate Tectonics
sections.description: Scientific theories explaining the formation, movement, and current positions of continents and oceans over geological time.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Proposed by German meteorologist Alfred Wegener in 1912.
scientific_principles.application: It suggests that millions of years ago, all continents were joined together in a single supercontinent called 'Pangaea', surrounded by a mega-ocean called 'Panthalassa'.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The Earth's lithosphere is divided into several major and minor tectonic plates floating over the semi-fluid asthenosphere.
scientific_principles.application: The continuous movement of these plates at their boundaries results in earthquakes, volcanism, trench formation, and mountain building.

sections.title: Continents of the World
sections.description: The 7 major landmasses on Earth and their distinct geographical characteristics.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest continent in terms of both area and population, covering about one-third of the Earth's total land area.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Located south of Europe, separated by the Mediterranean Sea.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: The second-largest continent. It is the only continent through which the Tropic of Cancer, the Equator, and the Tropic of Capricorn pass.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Located symmetrically around the South Pole.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is completely covered with thick ice sheets, hence known as the 'White Continent'. It has no permanent human settlements.

key_associations.extra_info: This mountain range naturally separates Europe from Asia. The combined landmass of Europe and Asia is called 'Eurasia'.
It is the world's longest mountain range, running from north to south along the western coast of the South American continent.

important_facts.fact: Australia is the smallest continent in the world and is completely surrounded by oceans on all sides, hence it is called an 'Island Continent'.

sections.title: Oceans of the World
sections.description: The major parts of the hydrosphere comprising massive bodies of salt water. There are 5 major oceans on Earth.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Spread between the Americas to the east and Asia/Australia to the west.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest and deepest ocean, covering one-third of the earth. Its shape is almost circular.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Located between the Americas and Europe/Africa.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the second-largest ocean, 'S' shaped, and the busiest ocean from the viewpoint of commerce and trade due to its highly indented coastline.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Located to the south of Asia and east of Africa.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the only ocean named after a country (India). Its shape is almost triangular.

important_facts.fact: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest ocean and is connected to the Pacific Ocean by a narrow stretch of shallow water known as the Bering Strait.
The continuous zone of active volcanoes and frequent earthquakes surrounding the Pacific Ocean is famously known as the 'Ring of Fire'.

sections.title: Ocean Floor Relief
sections.description: The physical topography of the ocean floor, which is as diverse, rugged, and irregular as the continental land surface.

key_concepts.explanation: The shallow, gently sloping, submerged extension of the continent. It is highly significant for fishing grounds, coral reefs, and petroleum extraction.
The deepest, narrow, and steep-sided depressions on the ocean floor. They are typically formed at subduction zones where one tectonic plate dives under another.
Massive underwater mountain ranges formed by plate tectonics at divergent boundaries, where magma upwells to create new oceanic crust.

key_associations.extra_info: It is the deepest known point on the Earth's surface, reaching a depth of about 11,034 meters (which is greater than the total height of Mount Everest).
